name: Lyo.Job.Workers.Notification
tagline: Job workers that send notifications as workflow steps: webhook POST, email, and SMS. A send that does not happen fails the run.
description:
Three `JobWorkerBase` implementations that turn notifying into a workflow step: `WebhookNotificationWorker` (`notification.webhook`), `EmailNotificationWorker` (`notification.email`), and `SmsNotificationWorker` (`notification.sms`).

These replace `JobDefinition.AlertWebhookUrl` and the per-definition alert columns. As a step, a notification can be conditional, can read upstream step results through templated parameters, and — the part a column could not do — **fails the job run when the send fails**, so the job system's retry, backoff, DLQ, and run-log history all apply.

Each worker declares its inputs as ordinary job parameters (`Url`, `Body`, `To`, `Subject`, ...), so one shared job definition per channel serves every workflow: the step's `ParametersJson` fills them in.

examples.title: Register in DI
Notify only when the load produced rows
examples.code:
JobWorkflowBuilder.New("Nightly ETL")
    .AddStep("Load", loadDefinitionId)
    .AddStep(
        "Notify", webhookDefinitionId,
        dependsOn: ["Load"],
        condition: JobWorkflowStepCondition.When("Load", "RowCount", ComparisonOperatorEnum.GreaterThan, "0"),
        parameters: new Dictionary<string, string> {
            ["Url"] = "https://hooks.example.com/etl",
            ["Body"] = "{\"rows\": \"{Step.Load.Result.RowCount}\"}"
        })
    .Build();

sections.title: Workers and their parameters
rows: `Headers` (JSON object of header name to value), `ContentType` (defaults to `application/json`)
sections.trail: `To` and `Cc` accept a comma or semicolon separated list. Values arrive already resolved: the scheduler formats a step's `ParametersJson` against the workflow context before creating the run, so `{Step.Extract.Result.RowCount}` is a number by the time the worker reads it.

sections.title: Why not INotificationPublisher
sections.text: `NotificationPublisher` catches and logs every handler exception by design, so routing through it would finish a run as `Success` even when nothing was delivered. That is the failure mode `JobDefinition.AlertWebhookUrl` had. These workers call `ILyoHttpClient`, `IEmailService`, and `ISmsService` directly, so a refused send is a failed run with the reason recorded in the run's results.

sections.title: Why not Lyo.Webhook
sections.text: `Lyo.Webhook` is inbound-only — signature verification and endpoint mapping for webhooks you receive. It has no sender, so the webhook worker uses `Lyo.Http.Client`.

sections.title: Retry and failure handling
sections.text: The webhook worker retries 408, 429, and 5xx responses plus transport errors `RetryCount` times with a doubling delay. Other 4xx responses fail immediately: a rejected payload is rejected identically every time. A missing required parameter fails the run without attempting a send, since a definition with no `Url` can never succeed no matter how often it is retried.
